name: Creality Falcon2 22W
tagline: 22W Entry Creality diode: simple upgrade path for 3D printer owners
tldr: Creality Falcon2 22W is the 22W SKU on the Creality creality falcon2 line. The base Falcon2 12W is Creality's affordable open-frame diode. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: Faster cutting and deeper hobby cuts while keeping solid engraving capability

priceRange.note: 22W optical module: verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: 10 mm basswood in one pass, per Creality
Integrated air assist for cleaner cuts
Creality claims colour marking on stainless steel with the right settings
cons: Open frame: goggles, ventilation and fire safety are up to you
Wider spot (about 0.10 mm) than lower-power diodes: very fine photo detail is softer
Thick hardwood and clear acrylic remain out of reach
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 22W SKU on Creality Falcon2. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Tune cut passes with air assist and focus checks. For photo engraving, slow down vs your cut presets: this head is optimized for throughput on wood, not only finesse.
primaryUse: Cut-biased diode tier for makers who outgrew 10–20W job times but stay on the same frame

editorialDepth.advantages: Creality Falcon2 22W targets mixed engraving and wood-cutting weeks: fewer passes on basswood and dark acrylic than weaker SKUs in the same line.
editorialDepth.limitations: Wrong pick if you never engrave and only wanted the lowest price. Ultra-fine photo work can look better on an engraving-first SKU. Open-frame: safety and smoke are on you.

faq.question: What can the Falcon2 22W cut in one pass?
faq.answer: Creality rates it at 10 mm basswood in one pass and 0.1 mm thin metal sheet; its own settings guide uses full power at 700 mm/min for 2 mm basswood. Our materials list stays at about 8 mm for clean, repeatable cuts.

faq.question: Falcon2 22W or 12W?
faq.answer: The 22W is the current model and fills a 10 × 10 cm photo in about 12–18 min against 17–26 min for the 12W in our benchmark. The 12W is discontinued; unless you find one used for far less, take the 22W.

faq.question: Is the 22W enough, or should I look at a 40W?
faq.answer: For ornaments, boxes in 3–6 mm plywood and engraving, the 22W is enough. Creality also sells a Falcon2 40W ($639 single unit, $739 Basic Kit in October 2026, against $589 for the 22W Basic Kit); it is worth the extra if you cut 10 mm stock every week.

standoutFeatures.title: 10 mm basswood in one pass
standoutFeatures.body: Creality rates the 22W module for 10 mm basswood in a single pass, which covers boxes, signs and ornaments in common plywood thicknesses.

standoutFeatures.title: Air assist built in
standoutFeatures.body: The integrated air assist clears smoke from the cut, for cleaner edges and less charring without buying a separate pump.
